answer: New agents receive only a tiny spending allowance until they earn trust through transactions with established participants. Each transaction locks a deposit; if a counterparty proves fraud, the deposit is forfeited and the agent loses access to future credit. An attacker can still create many identities, but each must fund a separate deposit and build a transaction history, tying up capital and time. An opal trader, timber broker, or harbor dispatcher cannot cheaply multiply influence by minting accounts alone.
